children: , which makes gallium nitride and silicon carbide power chips, rose 10.74% in premarket after it said the U.S. Army selected it for the ALATTIS program to develop next-generation 10 kV silicon carbide power semiconductors. The company didn't disclose the award's value.

The prototype project will develop and validate a domestic manufacturing process for ultra-high-voltage silicon carbide devices through design, fabrication and testing. Navitas said that process isn't currently available in the U.S. The program targets 10 kV insulated-gate bipolar transistors and related PiN diode technologies for mission-critical military systems, and it's sponsored by the Army Research Laboratory under the Army's Combat Capabilities Development Command.

For Navitas, the program pushes its silicon carbide business into higher voltages. Its current GeneSiC portfolio runs from 650 volts to 6.5 kV and is made through a U.S.-based supply chain. Chief Technology Officer Siddarth Sundaresan said the award lets Navitas "extend its leadership beyond SiC MOSFETs," building the new devices on its patented trench-assisted planar architecture.

title: Navitas Stock Jumps After U.S. Army Picks It for 10 kV Program
